summary: John Frederick Dickson was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Westminster School and completed his B.A. at Christ Church, Oxford, studying there from circa 1855 to 1859.

Active in Indology and linguistics, John Garrett became the first Direktor of the Central College of Bangalore in 1858 and served as Director of Public Instruction at Mysore's Department of Public Instruction in 1871.

John George Woodroffe worked in Indology and religious studies, studying at University College, Oxford, and under Sivachandra Vidyarnava. He held posts as Tagore Law Professor at Calcutta University (1897), Calcutta High Court Judge (c. 1904–1922), and Oxford Reader (1923–1930).

A scholar of Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, Hangin studied at Hokkaido, Columbia, and Indiana University. He taught at Johns Hopkins, Georgetown, UC Berkeley, Columbia, and was a full professor at Indiana University Bloomington (1965–1989).

John Graham Drummond worked in Indology and linguistics. He earned his B.A. (circa 1903–1906) and Ph.D. (by 1939) from Christ's College, Cambridge, where he also served as Lecturer in Bengali in 1936.

A historian and Indologist, John Greenfield Leonard earned degrees from Stanford (B.A., 1959) and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (M.A., 1962). He held appointments at Wisconsin-Madison in 1967 and the University of California, San Diego from 1968 to 1973.

An Indologist and art historian educated at the Royal College of Art, John Griffiths worked at the Victoria and Albert Museum, served as a professor at Sir Jamsetjee Jeejebhoy School of Art (1865), and was principal of the National College of Arts.
John H. Berthrong is a scholar of Sinology, philosophy, and religious studies who completed his graduate work under Alfonso Verdu. He held an attested post at Boston University in 1996.
Active in Sinology, John Hay received his M.A. from the University of Aberdeen by 1833. He later served as a fellow at the University of Madras from 1888 to 1889.

John Henry Hutton was an Indologist and historian educated at Chigwell School, Worcester College, and Oxford (D.Sc., 1921). He served in the Indian Civil Service (c. 1909–1937) and as Cambridge's William Wyse Professor of Social Anthropology (1936–1950).

Piet specialized in Indology, religious studies, and philosophy, earning degrees from Hope College, Western Theological Seminary, Hartford Seminary, and Columbia, alongside studies at Princeton Theological Seminary. He was Professor of English Bible and Mission at Western Theological Seminary (1960–1984).

A classicist and linguist, Wright studied at Dartmouth and Leipzig under Georg Curtius. He held posts at Ohio State (1873–1876), Dartmouth (1878–1886), Johns Hopkins (1886), Harvard (c. 1887–1908), and the American School of Classical Studies at Athens (1906–1907).

Specializing in Indology and history, John Herbert Harington served as secretary (1790) and president (1825–1828) of The Asiatic Society, as well as President of the Council of the College at Fort William College (c. 1801–1823).

John Hick worked in philosophy and religious studies. He held posts at Cornell, Princeton Theological Seminary, Cambridge, Birmingham, and served as Danforth Professor at Claremont Graduate University between 1985 and 1989.
John Hope studied at the University of Edinburgh from circa 1740 to 1750 and later held an academic post there from circa 1761 to 1786.

Crook worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. Educated at Southampton, Sherborne, and Cambridge under Robert Hinde and William Homan Thorpe, he studied under Sheng Yen and held posts at the University of Bristol (c. 1963–1995) and CASBS (c. 1968–1969).

John Irwin worked in Indology, history, and Buddhist studies. He was Assistant Keeper (1945) and Keeper (1959–1978) at the Victoria and Albert Museum, and served as Visiting Professor of the History of Indian Art at the University of Michigan in 1985.

Specializing in philosophy and Buddhist studies, John J. Holder studied under Harry Krebs. He held a visiting research post at Oxford and has served at St. Norbert College, where he was attested as Associate Professor of Philosophy in 2018.

A Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar, Makransky earned his PhD at Wisconsin-Madison (1981–1990) and studied under Geshe Lhundup Sopa. He held posts at Boston College (1992), Rangjung Yeshe Institute (2007), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies.

John James Jones was an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned an M.A. from Aberystwyth University (1911–1914). He served at the National Library of Wales as Assistant Keeper in 1926 and Deputy-Keeper in 1928.
